heading: Route size budgets
body:
A release build (`ty bundle`) checks how much script and WebAssembly each route loads. It starts at the page of the route and follows every file that the page loads: script tags, the modules of the services that the view uses, `import`s, `new URL(..., import.meta.url)` and other paths written as text in a script, and the file lists in JSON files that a script reads, such as .NET's `blazor.boot.json`. It does not count the service worker, and it cannot follow a path that a script builds while it runs.

The build writes Tachyon's own page scripts, such as `tac-client.js`, `behavior-runtime.js` and the shared script of each service language (`tachyon-rust.js`, `tachyon-go.js` and the others), without comment lines, indentation or blank lines, so a route carries less of them. The Go glue `wasm_exec.js` is written the same way, and it keeps its license notice. The code in each line stays as written, so an error in the browser still points at readable code.

The services that a route counts are the services that its views use and the services that those need. A JavaScript or TypeScript service needs another service when its file names the field that receives it, such as `middle;` or `this.middle = undefined`. When a service writes to `this` with a computed name (`this[key] = ...`, `Object.assign(this, ...)`), or hands `this` to a function from another file (`initialize(this)`, `helper.call(this)`, `const owner = this`), the build cannot know which services it needs, so every route that uses it counts every service of the project. Handing `this` to the service's own method is fine: `this.save.bind(this)` and `this.pick(id).call(this)` keep the list short. Each JavaScript or TypeScript service module also carries only the models that the service names, and the models that those name, not every models file of the project (ADR 0043, ADR 0074).

The sizes are the bytes that Tachyon sends: the Brotli copy when the build wrote one (see Compressed files), else the file itself. The build adds the `.js` and `.mjs` files and the `.wasm` files of each route and stops with `TY1337` when one total is over its budget. The error names the five biggest files, so you know what to split, drop or move to the server. Set the budgets in kilobytes in `client/manifest.json`: `tac.budgets.script` (default 200) and `tac.budgets.webassembly` (default 3584). A route with a Python service gets a script budget of 512 when `tac.python` is set and `tac.budgets.script` is not, because the copied Pyodide runtime brings its own scripts (ADR 0093). A route that loads more than one web runtime gets more script budget, but only for the runtimes it loads (ADR 0100). A web runtime is the browser side of a service language: .NET (C# and F# share it), Rust, Ruby, Lua, Java, Go, Dart, Kotlin, C++ or Swift. JavaScript and TypeScript are not runtimes; they are the page itself. Each runtime has a measured allowance, the script it adds as sent: .NET 96, Rust 92, Ruby 20, Lua 12, Java 12, Go 8, Dart 8, Kotlin 8, C++ 4 and Swift 4. The budget is 200 plus the allowance of every runtime the route loads except the largest one, because a single-language route already pays for its one runtime inside 200. So a route with C#, Rust and Go services gets 200 + 92 + 8 = 300, and a route with no runtime or one runtime keeps 200. When this budget is over, the error says how it was computed and which runtimes it counted. When you set `tac.budgets.script`, your value is the budget of every route and no allowance is added. `tac.budgets.check: false` turns the check off while a project migrates. `ty preview` does not check budgets, because it sends files without compression while it watches your sources (ADR 0074).

This website uses services in many languages, and the check counts all of them on each route, so its manifest raises the script budget to 320. It loads only the DuVay components that its views use: the full DuVay component bundle is 134 KiB as sent and put the documentation home over that budget.
